text.content:
The Wool-Crowned Warrens

Generations ago this was a way-station stable-yard, built by a shepherd-hermit named Old Tam to house pack animals passing through. Goblins moved into its bones long after he was gone and never left, and somewhere along the way they started worshipping the animals instead of just herding them - a joke, originally, about a drover who fell off a llama on a dare and wasn't spat at for it. That drover, Corvin Blackwell, is still here. He no longer looks entirely goblin, and he no longer entirely knows why.

The warren runs on a single, sincerely-held political principle: rank follows the favor of the herd, and especially of one llama, Buttercup, who now sits an actual throne of stacked saddlebags in the Larders while Corvin stands beside her and does the governing she has no interest in doing. The goblins see nothing strange in this. The party will.

Somewhere in the Larders, the warren's leadership is being quietly reshuffled based entirely on which goblins Buttercup nuzzles first - a live, ongoing process the party can watch play out on chalkboards and rumor throughout the floor (Rooms 1, 7, and 8 all reflect the current standings).

Tied to: Entrance (Room 0)

The Larders - once exactly that, a food store - have become equal parts throne room and petting zoo, and no goblin nominally in charge can explain when or how the shift happened. The party gets their first real look at it through the gap at the Corridor Junction (Room 6): a llama on a saddlebag throne, and a goblin-shaped something standing far too close beside it.

Tied to: Corridor Junction (Room 6)

The floor's story resolves in the Boss Arena: the Wool-Crowned King the goblins keep talking about is genuinely just Buttercup, beloved and harmless. The real threat is her "drover," Corvin Blackwell - a goblin who found something buried in Old Tam's old stable-yard, picked it up, and hasn't been entirely goblin, or entirely himself, since. The stairs down are behind his throne, past a ward that isn't goblin work at all.

Tied to: Boss Arena (Room 28)

Mudflap's Union. One llama has figured out that spitting on goblins earns double rations from a nervous administration eager to keep the herd happy, and has started training the rest of the pen in the technique - a small, self-inflicted crisis for the warren's already-thin food supply (Hazard Chamber, Room 3).

The Fixed Race. Two rival war-chiefs, Grull and Nak, have agreed to settle a feud with a llama race down the Larders' main hall - and have both been caught bribing the same racer, Spitfire, to throw it for them. Betting is open at the Treasure Vault (Room 4) and the Corridor Junction betting board (Room 18); the party is welcome to get involved.
